 Live Updates Updated Thu, Nov 19 2026 10:32 AM EST Share Share Article via Facebook Share Article via Twitter Share Article via LinkedIn Share Article via Email Anthropic’s Dario and Daniela Amodei join CNBC exclusively from the Nasdaq: IPO live updates
 Ashley Capoot This is CNBC live coverage of Anthropic's IPO and Nasdaq debut. 
 watch now VIDEO 5:16 05:16 Anthropic raises $81B+ in historic IPO: Here's what to know Squawk Box Anthropic is set for its long-awaited Nasdaq debut on Thursday, after the artificial intelligence lab raised over $81 billion in a record IPO , surpassing SpaceX 's offering in June. 
 The Claude creator sold 980 million shares at $83 a piece on Wednesday, lifting the size and price of its offering. Its fully diluted market cap sits at around $1.5 trillion.
 Tune in at 10:00 a.m. ET as Dario and Daniela Amodei join CNBC TV exclusively to talk about the debut. Watch in real time on CNBC+ or the CNBC Pro stream
 The 5-year-old company captivated the corporate world with its Claude AI models and products, which have fueled its meteoric rise this year. Anthropic said in its prospectus that it generated $33.24 billion in revenue for the nine months ended Sept. 30, up a staggering 1,200% from the same period last year.
 Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei co-founded the company in 2021 after he and a small group of researchers defected from OpenAI , now its chief rival. Anthropic has faced sharp criticism over its positions on safety, regulation and national security, including by President Donald Trump and other senior government officials. 
 The company will list on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol "ANT," and its debut will be a big test for the AI industry. Investors have been fretting over Jensen Huang's sudden ouster at Nvidia , voters' stinging rebuke of AI during the midterm elections and the feasibility of a multitrillion-dollar infrastructure buildout . 
 "Our aim is to help humankind chart a safe course through this technological evolution, open new frontiers of discovery, and bring forth an age of miracles," Anthropic's co-founders wrote in the company's prospectus. "Everyone who owns our stock, whether an institution or an individual, becomes part of that effort."
 Highlights so far:
 Dario Amodei addresses debt and landing an investment-grade credit rating
 Spotted: Executives sporting "Clawd" pins at Nasdaq
 Dario Amodei renews pledge to pace frontier AI development 
 Retail demand for ANT was the largest in history
 Anthropic employees set to get rich 
 Dario and Daniela Amodei arrive at the Nasdaq 
 CNBC's reporters are covering Anthropic's IPO live on air and online from our bureaus in San Francisco and Englewood Cliffs, New Jersey, and from the Nasdaq in New York City. 
 5 Min Ago No updates on clash with Pentagon
 Daniela Amodei said there were no significant updates on Anthropic's clash with Department to Defense but expects the company's relationship with the government to continue.
 "My feeling, honestly, at Anthropic is that we have always worked extremely well with the national security apparatus of the United States of America. We're very committed to ensuring that Claude is helping to protect the nation. We've had an incredible working relationship with with that entire part of the government, really since Anthropic was founded, and we expect that that will continue."
 — Caleigh Keating 
 9 Min Ago Dario Amodei says $900 billion commitments don't 'seem so large'
 Dario Amodei defended the company's massive $900 billion in AI commitments.
 "If you look at the amount of cash we have on the balance sheet and the amount of revenue that we're already making per year, suddenly those commitments don't seem so large," he said.
 Amodei said the company tries to "err on the low side" when predicting compute.
 — Samantha Subin 
 10 Min Ago Dario Amodei: Anthropic 'enjoying' working with SpaceX
 Dario Amodei, Co-Founder and CEO of Anthropic speaking with CNBC ahead of the Anthropic IPO on Nov. 19th, 2026. CNBC Dario Amodei said Anthropic is "enjoying" working with SpaceX amid speculation the company might scale back use of Elon Musk company's compute.
 "You can't be sure what you're going to do in the future. But you know, we're finding that compute to be to be high quality. We're enjoying working with SpaceX."
 — Caleigh Keating 
 10 Min Ago Amodeis decline to comment on whether Jensen Huang should return as Nvidia CEO
 Dario Amodei said Anthropic has had "a long and productive partnership" with Nvidia, but he and Daniela declined to comment on whether or not Jensen Huang should return as the company's CEO.
 — Ashley Capoot 
 11 Min Ago Dario Amodei: Anthropic hopes to secure investment-grade credit rating in future
 watch now VIDEO 3:33 03:33 Anthropic hopes to secure investment-grade credit rating in future, says CEO Dario Amodei Squawk on the Street Dario Amodei said Anthropic is "hoping" to secure an investment-grade credit rating in the future.
 "Obviously we will see how that turns out," he said.
 "Debt is an instrument that we have available to us, and we'd like to use at some point in the future," he added.
 — Ashley Capoot 
 11 Min Ago Daniela Amodei: Anthropic is a 'safety-first' company
 Daniela Amodei said Anthropic bears responsibility to ensure alignment within models and engage with consumers in order to mitigate risk.
 "The promise is incredible, and the risks are real. And we were really founded on this idea that it is our job to mitigate those risks, and I think we have to date done an incredible job doing that. We obviously have more work ahead of us, but we are deeply committed to safety."
 — Caleigh Keating 
 12 Min Ago Dario Amodei on pressure: "We've been calm about it"
 The pressure is on Anthropic with the expectations tied to being the largest IPO on record. 
 "We've been calm about it," CEO Dario Amodel said.
 Despite the turn in the spotlight, Amodei said the company is laser focused on the fundamentals.
 "We always want to under promise and over deliver," he said. "You know, that's our core."
 — Samantha Subin 
 16 Min Ago Daniela Amodei: Will listen to communities on data centers
 Daniela Amodei said the company is focusing on listening to consumers when it comes to data centers in the wake of the midterms.
 "One of the things that I think is really important to Anthropic is for it to feel to people like this technology is not happening to them. And I think really from our perspective, building data centers is something where we also need to listen to what it is that those communities want and help to bring forward that future as well."
 — Caleigh Keating 
 18 Min Ago Daniela Amodei: Anthropic's debut is 'one stop on the journey'
 Daniela Amodei said Anthropic is a "long-term focused company," so it thinks about its debut as just one step along its journey.
 "While today is a super exciting milestone, and we're obviously really, really excited about it, I think it's it's for us, it's like one stop on the journey," she said. "We think about this as, 'Wow, this is an incredible moment for Anthropic for our mission, but we're going to wake up tomorrow and we're going to be the same company.'"
 — Ashley Capoot 
 18 Min Ago Daniela Amodei talks public benefit structure
 Anthropic President Daniela Amodei touted the company's public benefit structure.
 "We're really trying to do something that we do think can have this incredible economic value and impact, but we want it to be baked into essentially our structure," she said.
 — Samantha Subin 
 21 Min Ago Dario Amodei: Balancing between growth and pacing a 'central tension'
 Dario Amodei said the balance between growth and pacing was one of the "central tensions" at the heart of Anthropic.
 "What we've done with pacing is essentially said, look, we could drive at 200 miles an hour. Maybe let's only drive at 90 miles an hour. Spend time figuring out how to do that safely, and the rest of that surplus we spend building the model in the right way."
 — Caleigh Keating 
 22 Min Ago Amodei on scaling laws: 'I don't think we really believed it until it actually happened'
 watch now VIDEO 3:52 03:52 Anthropic CEO on scaling laws: ‘I don’t think we really believed it until it actually happened’ Squawk on the Street Dario Amodei said while the scaling laws behind AI suggested the technology would become extremely capable, even he has been surprised to see it play out.
 "The scaling laws kind of imply that the technology and hopefully our work within it would would have this scale, but I don't think we really believed it until it actually happened," he said. "And it's happening right now."
 — Ashley Capoot 
 28 Min Ago Anthropic underwriters have the option to purchase up to an additional 147 million shares
 Anthropic said its underwriters have the option to purchase up to an additional 147 million shares of Class A common stock from the company, according to a Thursday filing , which would net the company another $12.2 billion. 
 Assuming that option is exercised, Anthropic would raise a total of $93.5 billion through its IPO, topping the $85.7 billion raised by SpaceX.
 Anthropic's underwriters have until Nov. to exercise the option.
 — Ashley Capoot 
 30 Min Ago Anthropic executives wear "Clawd" pins to ring opening bell
 A pin worn by CEO of Anthropic Dario Amodei inside the Nasdaq MarketSite ahead of the anticipated IPO of artificial intelligence company Anthropic in New York City on November 19, 2026. Charly Triballeau | Afp | Getty Images Anthropic executives were sporting "Clawd" pins while they rang the opening bell at the Nasdaq.
 Clawd is a pixelated crab mascot that the company associates with Claude Code, its popular AI coding product. 
 — Ashley Capoot 
 51 Min Ago Brad Gerstner: Anthropic not a 'get-rich-quick scheme'
 watch now VIDEO 8:16 08:16 Brad Gerstner on $5B Anthropic investment: A cornerstone investment for Altimeter Squawk Box Brad Gerstner, founder and CEO of Altimeter Captial, said Anthropic's ability to disprove profitability concerns and make their market debut despite recent headwinds and market pressures facing the tech industry demonstrated how "extraordinary" the company is.
 "I think this level of demand for the company from Altimeter and others, and from retail investors getting in the game, getting their shot on goal the first time, is real evidence of just how extraordinary this company has operated," Gerstner told CNBC's "Squawk Box."
 Gerstner's Altimeter Capital is planning on investing $5 billion in the AI lab, which he called a "cornerstone" investment for his firm.
 "This isn't a get-rich-quick scheme. As I've said, this will be a cornerstone investment for Altimeter. This is a multi-year compounder in the most important super cycle in the history of technology," Gerstner told CNBC.
 — Caleigh Keating 
 1 Hour Ago Amodei renews pledge to pace the development of AI in Nasdaq speech
 watch now VIDEO 5:14 05:14 Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei renews pledge to pace the development of AI in Nasdaq speech Squawk on the Street Amodei is speaking about AI's potential benefits and risks in his address at the Nasdaq. 
 He opened by talking about the technology's potential to advance medicine and cure diseases, and he reiterated the company's pledge to focus on safety pace the raining and advancement of AI systems.
 "Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so, only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing," Amodei said. "If we can show it's possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same."
 — Ashley Capoot 
 1 Hour Ago Daniela Amodei's message to people who fear AI
 Daniela Amodei, Co-founder and President of Anthropic speaks inside the Nasdaq MarketSite ahead of the anticipated IPO of artificial intelligence company Anthropic in New York City on November 19, 2026. Charly Triballeau | Afp | Getty Images Daniela Amodei spoke from the Nasdaq ahead of the opening bell, and had a message for people who are scared of AI.
 "This technology needs you — not your trust, not your use, but your voice," she said. "The end of this story isn't written yet. Intelligence is now something humans can build. What we choose to build with it is up to all of us."
 —Chris Eudaily 
 2 Hours Ago Retail demand for Anthropic's IPO was largest in history, sources tell CNBC
 watch now VIDEO 8:11 08:11 David Faber, CNBC insiders on what to watch from the Anthropic IPO today Squawk Box Retail demand for Anthropic's IPO was larger than demand for any other deal in history, sources told CNBC's David Faber.
 Anthropic targeted retail allocation of about 20%, as CNBC previously reported, a much higher percentage than the typical initial public offering, which is 5% to 10% for retail investors.
 Anthropic's stock could trade into the low $100s on Thursday, according to the people, who asked not to be named because they were not authorized to speak publicly.
 — Ashley Capoot 
 2 Hours Ago Over 400 Anthropic employees set to become centimillionaires
 watch now VIDEO 2:18 02:18 Anthropic's IPO could mint thousands of millionaires — and reshape San Francisco Tech The average Anthropic employee will be worth over $40 million after today's IPO, marking one of the most rapid wealth creation events in history. The AI lab has generated 1.77 billion employee options. Earlier hires stand to benefit even further, with over 400 employees expected to be worth $100 million or more at the current share price. 
 Lockup periods may alter the timeline for the gains to make it to the economy, but the newfound wealth is expected to supercharge the San Francisco real estate market and philanthropic giving.
 — Robert Frank, Caleigh Keating 
 2 Hours Ago Here's what it's like outside the Nasdaq
 Outside the Nasdaq ahead of the Anthropic IPO on Nov. 19th, 2026. Ashley Capoot | CNBC As of around 8:00 a.m. ET, the scene outside the Nasdaq is pretty sleepy, though there is some police presence. The Nasdaq isn't promoting Anthropic's logo yet, but there are some ads for Elon Musk's Grok Bot and the neocloud Nebius .
 — Ashley Capoot 
 2 Hours Ago Amodeis arrive at the Nasdaq
 Dario Amodei, chief executive officer of Anthropic PBC, and his wife Camilla Clark arrive for the Anthropic PBC initial public offering (IPO) at the Nasdaq MarketSite in New York, US, on Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026. Adam Gray | Bloomberg | Getty Images Daniela Amodei, co-founder and president of Anthropic PBC, arrives for the Anthropic PBC initial public offering (IPO) at the Nasdaq MarketSite in New York, US, on Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026. Adam Gray | Bloomberg | Getty Images Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and his sister, Anthropic President Daniela Amodei, have arrived at the Nasdaq in New York City.
 — Ashley Capoot 
 2 Hours Ago Anthropic IPO to surge 25% when it opens, perpetual futures indicate
 Anthropic PBC signage ahead of the company's initial public offering (IPO) at the Nasdaq MarketSite in New York, US, on Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026. Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty Images Anthropic is headed for a big first-day pop, if trading in the perpetual futures market is any indication. The futures in Anthropic on the Hyperliquid exchange were trading above $104, indicating a surge of more than 25% from its $83 IPO price.
 Anthropic trading in so-called perp futures on Polymarket were also showing a jump to similar levels. 
 "Early indications are that it's up about 25%," said J.J. Kinahan, senior VP of retail and alternative investments at CBOE Global Markets, on CNBC "Squawk Box." "With some of the tumultuous times here for Nvidia, a little bit of that trust has gone away from the retail investor so this is the way people I think are going to express themselves."
 Perpetual futures are a crypto-based new type of futures contract which never expire and don't represent any ownership in the companies its tracking. The derivatives correctly predicted the initial pop in the SpaceX IPO back in June. 
 Retail investors are clamoring to buy Anthropic in the open market, according to Vanda Research. Retail net buying will be about $250 million, double that of SpaceX buying, the firm estimates.
 — John Melloy 
 3 Hours Ago Tech giants buying $26 billion in Anthropic stock at IPO price
 Advanced Micro Devices , Broadcom , Google , Micron , Microsoft , Nvidia and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company are collectively investing $26 billion at the IPO price, a sign of the importance of Anthropic's offering to the entire tech industry. 
 — Ari Levy 
 3 Hours Ago Bigger than SpaceX
 Elon Musk and Andrew Ross Sorkin speak during the NY Times Dealbook Summit at Jazz at Lincoln Center, Nov. 18, 2026 in New York City. Adam Gray | Getty Images In June, SpaceX raised $75 billion in what was by far the largest IPO on record until Anthropic's share sale on Wednesday. Elon Musk's company ended up raising a total of $85.7 billion after underwriters exercised their overallotment.
 Anthropic is a major SpaceX customer, signing an agreement earlier this year "to spend an aggregate of up to $120.5 billion over terms extending into 2029, consisting of approximately $3.1 billion in the aggregate per month once all capacity has been delivered, which we expect in December 2026," according to the prospectus. 
 — Ari Levy 
 4 Hours Ago Academics and industry experts circulate ‘The MisAnthropic Statement’ ahead of listing
 More than 90 academics and AI safety experts signed " The MisAnthropic Statement " ahead of the company's Nasdaq debut, blasting it for amassing power and rushing to build potentially dangerous technology.
 "Anthropic warns that recursively self-improving AI could concentrate power and escape human control, yet races to build it first," the statement says. "The company uses safety branding to court investors, employees, and the public — even as it has quietly weakened its safety pledges and lobbied for self-serving regulation. Anthropic is not a safe AI company, and we must reject its reckless attempt to amass power in the name of the greater good."
 A representative for Anthropic declined to comment about the statement.
 — Ashley Capoot 
 5 Hours Ago Anthropic’s explosive revenue growth 
 The Anthropic Claude logo on a smartphone and laptop arranged in San Francisco, California, Nov. 10, 2026. David Paul Morris | Bloomberg | Getty Images Anthropic's revenue has surged dramatically this year as more companies have adopted its AI models and products. 
 The company said it generated roughly $33.24 billion in revenue for the nine months ended Sept. 30, up roughly 1,200% from the same period last year. 
 Anthropic's losses also widened, however. It reported a $104 billion net loss during the period, compared to a net loss of $25.1 billion over the same stretch in 2025. The vast majority of its loss, about $94.3 billion, comes from a change in fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities and SAFEs, Anthropic said.
 The company said its run-rate revenue was roughly $81 billion as of the end of October, up roughly $10 billion from the previous month.
 — Ashley Capoot 
 5 Hours Ago Anthropic’s seven co-founders have majority voting power 
 Zoom In Icon Arrows pointing outwards The founders of Anthropic. CNBC Anthropic said in its prospectus that it believes its seven co-founders are "distinctly equipped to be stewards of our mission." 
 The co-founders are the sole members of " Founder LLC ," a new entity that holds 50.1% of the voting power of the company's outstanding shares. The structure gives them "the ability to determine the outcome of all matters submitted to a vote of our stockholders generally for the foreseeable future," according to the filing.
 The co-founders' combined voting power from their holdings and their interest in Founder LLC is expected to be 61.3%, according to the filing.
 Here's who's calling the shots:
 Dario Amodei , Chief Executive Officer 
 Daniela Amodei, President 
 Tom Brown, Chief Compute Officer 
 Jack Clark, head of the Anthropic Institute 
 Jared Kaplan, Chief Science Officer 
 Sam McCandlish, Chief Architect 
 Christopher Olah, head of interpretability research efforts
 — Ashley Capoot
